SOURCE-COMMAND CORRECTION (important). The command in the brief, `git log --format='%cI %s' --since=2026-07-24 <branch> -- trace_out/`, returns only 22 landings, oldest 2026-07-24T19:17:52Z. That under-reports: git's --since date cutoff interacts with path-based history simplification and truncates the walk mid-range. Dropping --since and filtering by date in post (`git log --format='%cI %s' <branch> -- trace_out/`) yields 37 landings in the window, oldest 2026-07-24T02:38:18Z. All 15 landings the brief's command misses are real - verified each adds a trace_out/<stem>/batch_summary.part_NN.json via `git show --name-only`. Every number below uses the 37-landing set.

WHAT WAS COUNTED. Pairs per window are NOT inferred from consecutive offsets alone - I read len(results) out of each landed batch_summary.part_NN.json at its landing commit (`git show <sha>:<path>`), plus min/max of results[i].index. For the batches that ran to completion both methods agree exactly (17T: 8+20+8+7+19+8+15+15=100; 18T: 8+19+18+17+14+8+8+8=100; 14T contiguous 41-100=60; floor 50/50).

LANE SCOPE. The circuit-trace concurrency group carried two workloads that interleave, so both must appear or the idle gaps come out wrong. 29 windows traced 2panel PAIRS (342 rows). 8 windows traced the paraphrase-floor batch dialects_20260723T001434Z (38 rows; unit = baselines, not pairs). GROSS vs NET-NEW. 342 pair-traces delivered, but only 327 were pairs not already covered on the branch. 15 rows were re-traces: 13 at 2026-07-27T04:49:14Z (pairs_20260715T132350Z part_09 spans idx 9-23, but 11-23 were already in part_11, landed 2026-07-16T15:39:25Z - that window produced exactly 2 net-new pairs, 9 and 10, matching the journal's 89/100 -> 91/100), plus idx 37 at 19:17:52Z and idx 49 at 20:44:41Z in pairs_20260707T221438Z (both overlapping parts landed 2026-07-08). Dialect: 38 rows, 36 net-new (26-27 re-traced over part_26 from 2026-07-23). Full-lane net-new = 363 of 380.

IDLE CAUSE - THROTTLING vs RECLAIM (they are not the same failure). All three >3h gaps are container reclaims; none are 429s. Neuronpedia 429 throttling is heavily documented in the journal but only on 2026-07-24 (notes at 01:22:23Z, 01:23:11Z, 04:11:39Z, 05:37:43Z: 70-min step timeouts, '~10 pairs/window', '~4 baselines/window') - and 07-24 is the day with ZERO idle gaps, 19 landings on a steady 45-155 min cadence. Throttling shrank window YIELD; it never idled the lane. The idle came from losing the babysitter timer, leaving nobody to chain the next fire. The signature is mechanical and exact: each gap is immediately preceded by the only unresolved circuit-trace entries in the journal - (19:29:22Z, 21:00:32Z) before gap 1, (13:16:15Z, 14:49:32Z) before gap 2, (02:44:38Z, 04:15:22Z) before gap 3 - each landed its outputs but was never resolved or chained. In all three cases recovery came from the next scheduled daily backstop cycle (~13:15 UTC for gaps 1-2, 18:35 for gap 3).

A 3rd reclaim is named in the journal (2026-07-26T21:10:45Z, 'lane restart after 3rd container reclaim') but produced NO idle gap - landings continued 20:54 -> 22:12 -> 22:58 - because the session restarted inside the ~75-min window. So 4 reclaims, 3 idle gaps.

QUEUE HEALTH. 39 circuit-trace fires in the window, all $0 (no max_spend field on any entry), zero evictions (evicted:false throughout), 37 landings + 2 fires in flight at cutoff = 39. Every fire produced exactly one landing commit; the one-running + one-pending discipline held with no silent pending-slot eviction.
